newsitem.title: UK: Equal opportunities key to business success - UK CBI.
newsitem.headline: Equal opportunities key to business success - UK CBI.

text.p: More UK companies should make equal opportunities for workers fundamental to their strategy, the Confederation of British Industry said on Tuesday.
It said small- and medium-sized enterprises have as much to gain from incorporating equal opportunities as large companies.

"Effective equal opportunity practices achieve increased flexibility and competitiveness, and improve morale at work and in the wider community," said Tony Ward, chairman of the CBI's equal opportunities panel.
Ward was speaking at the launch of a CBI initiative, "A Winning Strategy - the Business Case for Equal Opportunities".
"There is no case for discrimination in the workplace based on characteristics which bear no relation to an individual's ability and potential to do the job," Ward said.
The CBI applauded existing schemes by National Westminster Bank Plc, Shell UK, British Telecommunications Plc and J. Sainsbury Plc.
Herman Ousely, chairman of the Commission for Racial Equality welcomed the CBI initiative. "The CRE looks for...the CBI to be a lead in implementing practical action," he said.

John Monks, general secretary of the Trades Union Congress added: "As British world-class companies testify, valuing diversity and promoting equal opportunities benefits both employees and business. I hope this initiative will encourage others to follow their lead."
